title: Real phase retrieval and phaseless ambiguity

items.title: The Vandermonde determinant for real moment-curve vectors

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.013A, Chapter B §1, The Vandermonde Determinant

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, let $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ be commuting indeterminates over $\mathbb R$, and let $V_d$ be the $d\times d$ matrix with $(i,j)$ entry $t_j^{i-1}$. Then
$$\det V_d=\prod_{1\le p<q\le d}(t_q-t_p).$$
Consequently, for any distinct real numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_d$, the $d$ vectors
$$(1,s_j,s_j^2,\ldots,s_j^{d-1})^{\mathsf T},\qquad 1\le j\le d,$$
are linearly independent.

items.title: Real phase retrieval via finite real measurements

references.title: Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006), arXiv:math/0412411
Philipp Grohs, Sarah Koppensteiner, and Martin Rathmair, Phase Retrieval: Uniqueness and Stability, arXiv:1901.07911v2
Radu Balan, Frames and Phaseless Reconstruction, full lecture notes (2015)

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $m\ge0$, and $\Phi=(a_i)_{i\in[m]}$ be a finite family in $\mathbb R^d$, allowing zero measurement vectors and not assuming that $\Phi$ spans. Here $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $[0]=\varnothing$; measurement labels are one-based, while coordinates in $\mathbb R^d$ use the library's zero-based convention $k<d$. Write $\mathbb R^{[m]}=\{y:[m]\to\mathbb R\}$. Use the Euclidean inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_{k<d}u_kv_k$ and norm $\|u\|_2=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle}$. Define the signal equivalence relation $x\sim z$ by $z=x$ or $z=-x$, let $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/\sim$, and write $q(x)=[x]$. Its quotient distance is
$$d_{\pm}([x],[z]):=\min\{\|x-z\|_2,\|x+z\|_2\}.$$

Use data space $Y_m=\{b:[m]\to[0,\infty)\}$ with metric
$$\rho_m(b,c)=\begin{cases}\sqrt{\sum_{k<m}(b_{k+1}-c_{k+1})^2},&m\ge1,\\0,&m=0.\end{cases}$$
The fixed relabeling $i\mapsto i-1$ identifies $[m]$-indexed data with the library's zero-based $\mathbb R^m$; $Y_0$ is a singleton. Define the real analysis map $T_\Phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{[m]}$ by
$$T_\Phi x=(\langle a_i,x\rangle)_{i\in[m]}.$$
The amplitude map is $\mathcal M_\Phi([x])=(|\langle a_i,x\rangle|)_{i\in[m]}$, while the intensity map is
$$\mathcal I_\Phi([x])=(\langle a_i,x\rangle^2)_{i\in[m]}\in Y_m.$$
A finite real measurement family performs **phase retrieval** when $\mathcal I_\Phi:Q_d\to Y_m$ is injective, equivalently when the induced amplitude map is injective. The quotient distance, both induced maps, and the data metric are well defined as verified below.

The diagram records the identity $\mathcal I_\Phi\circ q=S\circ T_\Phi$, where $S(y)=(y_i^2)_{i\in[m]}$ is coordinatewise squaring. It distinguishes signed linear measurements, amplitudes, and intensities; no proof relies on the diagram.

```tikzcd
\mathbb R^d \arrow[r,"T_\Phi"] \arrow[d,"q"'] & \mathbb R^{[m]} \arrow[d,"S"] \\
Q_d \arrow[r,"\mathcal I_\Phi"'] & [0,\infty)^m
```

items.title: The real sign quotient and its induced measurement maps

references.title: Philipp Grohs, Sarah Koppensteiner, and Martin Rathmair, Phase Retrieval: Uniqueness and Stability, arXiv:1901.07911v2, quotient metric discussion
Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006)

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $m\ge0$, and $\Phi=(a_i)_{i\in[m]}$ be a family in $\mathbb R^d$. Define $x\sim z$ by $z=x$ or $z=-x$, let $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/\sim$, and put
$$d_{\pm}([x],[z])=\min\{\|x-z\|_2,\|x+z\|_2\}.$$
Let $Y_m=\{b:[m]\to[0,\infty)\}$ carry the metric induced from zero-based Euclidean $\mathbb R^m$ by the fixed relabeling $i\mapsto i-1$ when $m\ge1$, and the zero metric on the singleton $Y_0$ when $m=0$. Define
$$\mathcal M_\Phi([x])=(|\langle a_i,x\rangle|)_{i\in[m]},\qquad \mathcal I_\Phi([x])=(\langle a_i,x\rangle^2)_{i\in[m]}.$$
Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation, $d_{\pm}$ is a metric on $Q_d$, $Y_m$ is a metric space, and both displayed measurement maps are well defined. Moreover, $\mathcal I_\Phi$ is coordinatewise the square of $\mathcal M_\Phi$, so the two maps are injective simultaneously.

items.title: Complement property for a real finite measurement family

references.title: Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006), §2
Philipp Grohs, Sarah Koppensteiner, and Martin Rathmair, Phase Retrieval: Uniqueness and Stability, arXiv:1901.07911v2, §2.1

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $m\ge0$, and let $\Phi=(a_i)_{i\in[m]}$ be a finite family in $\mathbb R^d$. For $S\subseteq[m]$, write
$$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\Phi_S):=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{a_i:i\in S\},$$
with $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\Phi_{\varnothing})=\{0\}$. The family $\Phi$ has the **complement property** if for every $S\subseteq[m]$,
$$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\Phi_S)=\mathbb R^d \quad\text{or}\quad \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\Phi_{[m]\setminus S})=\mathbb R^d.$$
The definition applies to labeled families, including repeated or zero vectors.

items.title: Full-spark real measurement families

references.title: Radu Balan, Frames and Phaseless Reconstruction, full lecture notes (2015), §3.2
Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006), Corollary 2.6

items.statement: Let $d\ge1$, $m\ge d$, and let $\Phi=(a_i)_{i\in[m]}$ be a finite family in $\mathbb R^d$. The family is **full spark** if for every list of distinct labels $i_1,\ldots,i_d\in[m]$, the vectors $a_{i_1},\ldots,a_{i_d}$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb R$.

items.title: Finite sign enumeration for real phase retrieval

references.title: Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006)
Philipp Grohs, Sarah Koppensteiner, and Martin Rathmair, Phase Retrieval: Uniqueness and Stability, arXiv:1901.07911v2

items.statement:
Input a real measurement matrix $A$ with $m$ rows indexed by $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $d$ columns indexed by $k<d$, where $d\ge1$ and $m\ge0$. Use row $i-1$ of the ordinary zero-based $m\times d$ matrix for measurement label $i$. Input nonnegative intensities $b:[m]\to[0,\infty)$, a mode in $\{\mathrm{exact},\mathrm{noisy}\}$, a feasibility tolerance $\varepsilon\ge0$, a maximum sign-pattern count $P\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, and a linear-solve budget $L\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. Put $r_i=\sqrt{b_i}$.

For $m=0$, let $\mathcal S_m$ contain only the empty sign vector. For $m\ge1$, let
$$\mathcal S_m=\{s:[m]\to\{-1,+1\}:s_1=+1\},$$
ordered lexicographically with $+1$ before $-1$ and labels in increasing order. This gives one representative from each pair $\{s,-s\}$. A signed right-hand side is $y_s=(s_i r_i)_{i\in[m]}$, interpreted in the same zero-based row order as $A$.

If $P=0$ or $L=0$, return no candidates with status budget-exhausted. Otherwise compute one SVD of $A$, form its unique Moore–Penrose inverse $A^+$ and kernel $\ker A$, then process at most the first $P$ patterns in $\mathcal S_m$ and perform at most $L$ signed least-squares solves. Stop when either budget is exhausted. For each processed pattern $s$, compute the minimum-Euclidean-norm least-squares solution $x_s=A^+y_s$ and signed residual $e_s=\|Ax_s-y_s\|_2$. The budget $L$ counts right-hand-side solves after the one SVD factorization.

* In exact mode, record the affine family $x_s+\ker A$ when $e_s\le\varepsilon$, together with $e_s$. Mark it exact-feasible if $e_s=0$ and tolerance-feasible if $0<e_s\le\varepsilon$. If $\varepsilon=0$ and all patterns are processed, return the union of the exact-feasible families modulo $x\sim -x$, or report infeasible if this union is empty. For $\varepsilon>0$, report only the tolerance-qualified least-squares families; this is a tolerance screen, not a list of every vector whose residual is at most $\varepsilon$.
* In noisy mode, initialize the incumbent as unset. For the first processed pattern, store $x_s$ and $J(x_s)$. For each later processed pattern, replace the incumbent by $x_s$ exactly when $J(x_s)$ is strictly smaller than the incumbent value; on a tie, keep the earlier pattern. Thus the incumbent has smallest $J$ among all processed candidates.
  Compute each visited candidate's squared amplitude residual
  $$J(x_s)=\sum_{i\in[m]}(|(Ax_s)_i|-r_i)^2$$
  before applying that update. The feasibility tolerance is not used in this mode.
* Return the candidates and a status. Exact mode returns exact-feasible/infeasible only when $\varepsilon=0$ and all patterns are processed; positive tolerance returns tolerance-feasible/no-tolerance-fit when all patterns are processed. Noisy mode returns a completed best candidate when all patterns are processed. If either budget stops enumeration before all patterns are processed, return budget-exhausted with any candidates found. A budget-exhausted result makes no claim about unvisited patterns.
* There are $1$ canonical pattern for $m=0$ and $2^{m-1}$ for $m\ge1$. Full enumeration is exponential in $m$. No statistical optimality or intensity-noise guarantee is part of this algorithm.

items.title: Real phase retrieval is equivalent to the complement property

references.title: Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006), Theorem 2.8
Philipp Grohs, Sarah Koppensteiner, and Martin Rathmair, Phase Retrieval: Uniqueness and Stability, arXiv:1901.07911v2, Theorem 2.2 and proof
Radu Balan, Frames and Phaseless Reconstruction, full lecture notes (2015), Theorem 3.2

items.statement: Let $d\ge1$, $m\ge0$, $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ with $[0]=\varnothing$, and let $\Phi=(a_i)_{i\in[m]}$ be a finite family in $\mathbb R^d$. Use the standard dot product $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_{k<d}u_kv_k$, identify $x,z\in\mathbb R^d$ when $z=x$ or $z=-x$, and write $[x]$ for the resulting class. Define $\mathcal I_\Phi([x])=(\langle a_i,x\rangle^2)_{i\in[m]}$, a formula independent of the representative because replacing $x$ by $-x$ leaves every square unchanged. For $S\subseteq[m]$, let $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\Phi_S)$ be the set of finite real linear combinations of its vectors, with the empty span equal to $\{0\}$. Then $\mathcal I_\Phi$ is injective on the global-sign classes if and only if for every $S\subseteq[m]$ at least one of $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\Phi_S)$ and $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\Phi_{[m]\setminus S})$ equals $\mathbb R^d$.

items.title: Correctness and amplitude-residual objective of finite sign enumeration

references.title: Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006), §2
Philipp Grohs, Sarah Koppensteiner, and Martin Rathmair, Phase Retrieval: Uniqueness and Stability, arXiv:1901.07911v2, §§1–2.1

items.statement: Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}$, $d\ge1$, $m\ge0$, with rows labeled $i=1,\ldots,m$ and signal coordinates labeled $k<d$, and let $b:[m]\to[0,\infty)$. Denote row $i-1$ by $a_i$ and put $\Phi=(a_i)_{i\in[m]}$. Define $[x]$ using $x\sim -x$ and $\mathcal I_\Phi([x])=((Ax)_i^2)_{i\in[m]}$. Put $r_i=\sqrt{b_i}$. Use the sign set consisting of the empty pattern when $m=0$ and otherwise the patterns $s:[m]\to\{-1,+1\}$ with $s_1=+1$, ordered lexicographically with $+1$ before $-1$. For each pattern put $y_s=(s_i r_i)_{i\in[m]}$, let $x_s=A^+y_s$ be the minimum-norm least-squares solution, and let $e_s=\|Ax_s-y_s\|_2$. Here $A^+$ is the unique Moore–Penrose inverse and $\ker A=\{v:Av=0\}$. The algorithm processes patterns in order subject to a maximum pattern count $P\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and signed-solve budget $L\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$; an early stop returns status budget-exhausted. In exact mode with tolerance $\varepsilon=0$, after every pattern is processed it returns the union of the exact families $x_s+\ker A$ modulo global sign, or reports infeasible if that union is empty. For every processed pattern, $x_s$ minimizes $\|Ax-y_s\|_2$, and the complete set of signed least-squares minimizers is $x_s+\ker A$; this set solves $Ax=y_s$ exactly if and only if its residual $e_s$ is zero. The complete exact-mode output is exactly $\{[x]:\mathcal I_\Phi([x])=b\}$. In noisy mode the algorithm scores $J(x)=\sum_{i\in[m]}(|(Ax)_i|-r_i)^2$ and, after every canonical pattern is processed, returns a candidate minimizing $J$ over all $x\in\mathbb R^d$. When a budget stops enumeration early, the returned candidates describe only processed patterns and give no completeness or global-minimum guarantee. For $m=0$, the single pattern has the unique empty right-hand side and $J(x)=0$ for every $x$.

items.title: The sharp real phase-retrieval count for full-spark measurements

references.title: Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006), Corollaries 2.6–2.7
Radu Balan, Frames and Phaseless Reconstruction, full lecture notes (2015), Corollary 3.3
MIT OpenCourseWare 18.013A, Chapter B §1, Vandermonde determinant

items.statement: Let $d\ge1$, $m\ge0$, and let $\Phi=(a_i)_{i\in[m]}$ be a finite family in $\mathbb R^d$, with $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $[0]=\varnothing$. Write $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_{k<d}u_kv_k$. If $m\le2d-2$, then there are $x,z\in\mathbb R^d$ with $z\ne x$ and $z\ne-x$ but $\langle a_i,x\rangle^2=\langle a_i,z\rangle^2$ for every $i\in[m]$. If $m\ge2d-1$ and every list of $d$ distinct measurement labels indexes linearly independent vectors, then equality of all these squared measurements implies $z=x$ or $z=-x$. For every $d\ge1$, this count is attained at $m=2d-1$: for any distinct real numbers $t_1,\ldots,t_m$, the vectors $a_i=(1,t_i,t_i^2,\ldots,t_i^{d-1})^{\mathsf T}$ satisfy the stated independence condition and hence the squared measurements determine the signal up to global sign.

title: Real phase retrieval and phaseless ambiguity — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Translation and reflection ambiguities for a finite Fourier magnitude map

references.title: Philipp Grohs, Sarah Koppensteiner, and Martin Rathmair, Phase Retrieval: Uniqueness and Stability, arXiv:1901.07911v2, Proposition 3.3

items.statement: Let $C_3=\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z$, put $\omega=(-1-i\sqrt3)/2$, and for a real signal $f:C_3\to\mathbb R$ define its unnormalised discrete Fourier transform by $\widehat f(k)=\sum_{n=0}^{2}f(n)\omega^{kn}$ for the representatives $k=0,1,2$. Its Fourier magnitude data are $(|\widehat f(k)|)_{k=0}^{2}$. Define translation by $(\tau_1 f)(n)=f(n-1)$ and reflection by $(Rf)(n)=f(-n)$, with indices in $C_3$. For $f(0)=1$, $f(1)=2$, and $f(2)=0$, both $\tau_1f$ and $Rf$ have the same Fourier magnitude data as $f$, while neither equals $f$ or $-f$.

items.title: A two-vector real family with a failed partition and an ambiguous pair

references.title: Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006), the partition construction in the converse proof of Theorem 2.8
Radu Balan, Frames and Phaseless Reconstruction, full lecture notes (2015), Theorem 3.2 proof

items.statement: In $\mathbb R^2$ with $u\cdot v=u_1v_1+u_2v_2$, take the real measurement family $\Phi=(a_1,a_2)$ with $a_1=(1,0)$ and $a_2=(0,1)$, and define its intensity data by $I_\Phi(x)=((a_1\cdot x)^2,(a_2\cdot x)^2)$. The partition $S=\{1\}$ has neither side spanning $\mathbb R^2$. The signals $x=(1,1)$ and $z=(-1,1)$ satisfy neither $z=x$ nor $z=-x$, but $I_\Phi(x)=I_\Phi(z)$.

items.title: A one-pattern sign budget misses the best amplitude fit
items.statement: Let $d=1$, $m=2$, $A=(1,-1)^{\mathsf T}$, and $b=(1,4)$, so $r=(1,2)$. In noisy sign enumeration, fix the first sign to $+1$, order the remaining signs with $+1$ before $-1$, and use $P=L=1$. The algorithm processes only $(+1,+1)$, returns $x=-1/2$ with $J(x)=\sum_{i=1}^2(|(Ax)_i|-r_i)^2=5/2$, and reports budget-exhausted. The unprocessed pattern $(+1,-1)$ has least-squares candidate $x=3/2$ with $J(x)=1/2$.

items.title: A two-dimensional three-vector full-spark real frame

references.title: Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, full-spark phase retrieval threshold, Corollary 2.6
Radu Balan, Frames and Phaseless Reconstruction, full lecture notes (2015), Corollary 3.3

items.statement: In $\mathbb R^2$ take $\Phi=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ with $a_1=(1,0)$, $a_2=(0,1)$, and $a_3=(1,1)$. Its intensity map on classes modulo $x\sim -x$ is $[x]\mapsto(x_1^2,x_2^2,(x_1+x_2)^2)$. Every pair is linearly independent, so every pair spans $\mathbb R^2$; consequently, for every partition one side spans $\mathbb R^2$. Equality of the displayed triples therefore forces two signals to be equal up to a global sign.

items.title: The complement property is not sufficient for complex phase retrieval

references.title: Philipp Grohs, Sarah Koppensteiner, and Martin Rathmair, Phase Retrieval: Uniqueness and Stability, arXiv:1901.07911v2, complex-field discussion in §2.1
Radu Balan, Pete Casazza, and Dan Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 20(3) (2006), discussion following Theorem 2.8

items.statement: In $\mathbb C^2$ use $a_1=(1,0)$, $a_2=(0,1)$, and $a_3=(1,1)$, and define $\langle a,x\rangle=\overline{a^{(1)}}x_1+\overline{a^{(2)}}x_2$ for $a=(a^{(1)},a^{(2)})$. Identify signals by global phase, $x\approx z$ when $z=\lambda x$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ with $|\lambda|=1$, and use intensity data $(|\langle a_j,x\rangle|^2)_{j=1}^3$. Here the complex complement property means that every subset of the three labels or its complement spans $\mathbb C^2$. Each pair spans $\mathbb C^2$, so the family has this property; nevertheless, $x=(1,i)$ and $z=(1,-i)$ have equal intensity data and are not related by a global phase. Thus the real complement-property criterion and its real full-spark count cannot be transferred to complex phase retrieval.
